title: When InVenture Went From Scoring Borrowers to Lending to Them
conflicts: Slate's 'research non-profit' is not supported: InVenture was a venture-backed company whose first product was finance tracking and licensed credit data (TechCrunch 2014); Siroya says it was often mistaken for a nonprofit. Early loan volumes and repayment figures differ widely between TechMoran, TED, Business Daily and HapaKenya; none is used. Pricing differs by date (5-11%, 11-15%, 15% for 30 days); the story uses Reuters' 2018 finding with the company's response.
notes: Criticism is reported attributed, as asked: Reuters (via The Star) equated a month's loan at 15 per cent to 180 per cent a year; Tala said rates fall with repayment and its East Africa manager called annualised comparisons malicious. Data-use concerns are reported as the sector-wide concerns behind the 2022 CBK licensing (TechCabal), with Tala's own statement that it never sells data or calls contacts; no finding against Tala specifically was found. Founding year (2011 vs 2012) and UN research dates (2006-08 vs 2007-09) conflict and are omitted. Boston Review, Forbes, Inc. and Fast Company are blocked; an unlicensed copy of an FT profile was read but not cited. Stance 'complicates'.
